title: How can congruent triangles give the other two sides?
description: A diagonal cuts the parallelogram into two triangles. Opposite angles, alternate angles and the shared diagonal make them congruent, so the missing sides copy the given ones. Keeko doubts the order of letters in a congruence.
teaching_notes: One idea: two triangles made by a diagonal are congruent, so the opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal. Watch for students who write the letters of a congruence in an order that pairs the wrong corners.

source: In parallelogram ABCD, AB = 4 cm and AD = 5 cm. Find CB and CD.
video_script.why: The child sees that a diagonal gives two congruent triangles, so the unknown sides equal the opposite sides.
video_script.substitution: the book's own parallelogram with AB = 4 cm and AD = 5 cm
video_script.anchor: the parallelogram ABCD of the book with AB = 4 cm and AD = 5 cm
video_script.wrong_answer: triangle eigh B D is congruent to triangle C B D
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko writes triangle ABD is congruent to triangle CBD, which pairs AB with CB, but AB is 4 cm and CB is 5 cm.
video_script.payoff_line: C B is five centimetres and C D is four centimetres

final_answer.spoken: C B is five centimetres and C D is four centimetres

never_show: the order ABD and CBD written as a correct congruence
maths_rules: diagonal BD splits ABCD into triangle ABD and triangle CDB
angle BAD = angle DCB (opposite angles of a parallelogram)
AD || BC with transversal BD: angle ADB = angle CBD (alternate angles)
BD is common, so triangle ABD is congruent to triangle CDB by AAS
CB = AD = 5 cm and CD = AB = 4 cm
triangle ABD to triangle CBD would pair AB with CB, 4 cm against 5 cm
video_script.design: One idea: a diagonal makes two congruent triangles. One parallelogram stays on the board and the two triangles are coloured in turn.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; the parallelogram ABCD with AB = 4 cm and AD = 5 cm marked and the other two sides shown as question marks

marks.sides: the two given sides are marked
marks.ask: question marks appear on the other two sides

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about a parallelogram.
<bookmark mark='sides'/>Two neighbouring sides are four centimetres and five centimetres.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>The other two sides are not given.
Which of them do you think are four centimetres long?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the parallelogram with the line from B to D drawn; the two triangles coloured; the words diagonal and congruent

marks.diag: the line B D is drawn
marks.cong: the two triangles slide on top of each other and match

narration: <bookmark mark='diag'/>A line joining two opposite corners of a four-sided shape is called a diagonal.
<bookmark mark='cong'/>Two triangles that match exactly are called congruent.

beats.on_screen: Given: ABCD is a parallelogram, AB = 4 cm, AD = 5 cm
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, eigh B C D is a parallelogram.
Side eigh B is four centimetres and side eigh D is five centimetres.
<bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find C B and C D.

beats.on_screen: Join diagonal BD. ∠BAD = ∠DCB (opposite angles of a parallelogram)

marks.join: the diagonal B D is drawn
marks.opp: angle A and angle C light up in one colour

narration: <bookmark mark='join'/>Step one, join the diagonal B D, and look at triangles eigh B D and C D B.
<bookmark mark='opp'/>Opposite angles of a parallelogram are equal, so angle B eigh D equals angle D C B.

marks.par: sides A D and B C are traced as parallels
marks.alt: angle A D B and angle C B D light up in a second colour

narration: <bookmark mark='par'/>Step two, eigh D and B C are parallel, and B D cuts them.
<bookmark mark='alt'/>The alternate angles are equal, so angle eigh D B equals angle C B D.

beats.on_screen: BD is common: ∆ABD ≅ ∆CDB (two angles and a side)

marks.com: diagonal B D glows as the shared side
marks.rule: the two triangles are matched corner by corner

narration: <bookmark mark='com'/>Step three, B D is common to both triangles.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>By the angle angle side rule, triangle eigh B D is congruent to triangle C D B.

beats.on_screen: matching sides: CB = AD = 5 cm; CD = AB = 4 cm

marks.match: the matching sides light up in pairs
marks.cb: C B is set equal to eigh D
marks.cdv: C D is set equal to eigh B

narration: <bookmark mark='match'/>Step four, matching sides of congruent triangles are equal.
<bookmark mark='cb'/>C B equals eigh D, which is five centimetres.
<bookmark mark='cdv'/>C D equals eigh B, which is four centimetres.

beats.on_screen: Answer: CB = 5 cm and CD = 4 cm
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>C B is five centimetres and C D is four centimetres.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: ∆ABD ≅ ∆CBD written and crossed out; arrows from A to C and B to B; AB = 4 cm against CB = 5 cm

marks.pair: arrows show which corners it pairs
marks.fix: four centimetres and five centimetres are shown unequal

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks triangle eigh B D is congruent to triangle C B D.
<bookmark mark='pair'/>That order pairs eigh with C and B with B, so it says eigh B equals C B.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But eigh B is four centimetres and C B is five, so the order is wrong.
The letters must follow the matching corners.
